subject: MediCore streaming pauses, proxy aggregation and chunking causing timeouts
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@medicorehealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:04 -0700
Subject: Live inference stream stalls during bulk upload

Diego / Redwood team,

We hit a severe problem last night during our nightly batch ingestion (approx 02:00 UTC). While streaming responses to our client UIs, token output pauses for ~30-60s intermittently and then either resumes a few tokens at a time or closes the socket with an EOF. The client automatically retries, which floods your endpoint with reconnects and causes a cascade of 502/504 errors.

Impact summary: 
- Affected services: live-qa, assistance-chat (prod clusters a/b/c)
- Duration: recurring bursts between 01:50–03:30 UTC
- User-visible: sessions dropping; average response latency spiked from ~120ms to >2s during pauses
- Error delta: 7x increase in 5xxs during the window

We captured app logs, connection IDs, and a network trace. Attaching a tar with server logs and a short pcap. Can you confirm whether any recent routing/proxy changes or kernel/IO patches were rolled out around 03:00 UTC? This is urgent — our C-level is asking for an explanation and a mitigation plan now.

Attachments: medicore_logs_20280328.tar.gz (logs), proxy_pcap_0328.pcap (pcap)

Thanks,
Lena Park
SRE, MediCore Health

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@medicorehealth.com>, Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:25:13 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference stream stalls during bulk upload

Thanks for the heads up, Lena — we see the ticket and the attachments. I'm spinning up a short triage thread here and looping SRE and CS.

Initial ask for SRE (David): please pull the proxy/edge logs for MediCore routing (route id: medcore-prod) between 01:30–03:45 UTC, and grep for connection close reasons and chunk coalescing metrics. Also surface any config changes or host reboots pushed during that window.

Short-term mitigations to try immediately (low risk):
- Route MediCore traffic to bypass the edge aggregator (bypass-proxy) to test direct host routing.
- Increase WS ping interval and drop the client-side keepalive threshold to avoid early EOFs.
- Temporarily pin users to a lower concurrency/streaming batch size (we can toggle via feature flag).

I'll notify leadership if we see customer-impact wide enough to require credits or SLA exception. Please keep customer and Tim in the loop.

— Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@medicorehealth.com>, Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:40:57 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference stream stalls during bulk upload

On Wed, Mar 28, 2028 at 9:25 AM Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial ask for SRE (David): please pull the proxy/edge logs for MediCore routing (route id: medcore-prod) between 01:30–03:45 UTC, and grep for connection close reasons and chunk coalescing metrics.

Got it. Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the initial log sweep and pcap: 
- Around 03:05 UTC we had a rolling config push to the proxy cluster that changed the chunk coalescing timer (intended to improve throughput for small messages). The change increased the aggregation window from 5ms -> 40ms.
- When tight client-side keepalive/short-lived streams intersect with aggregated server-side chunks, we observe connection stalls: the proxy buffers tokens and doesn't flush until the timer fires, which appears as a ~30–60s silence for in-flight websockets in some edge cases when retries/slow clients re-negotiate streams.
- There is also evidence of file descriptor exhaustion on one host (edge-03) during the storm — descriptors were at 92% until the host started dropping accepts.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Rolled back the chunk coalescing change at 09:32 PT (03:32 UTC) for mediсore-prod route only.
- Enabled bypass-proxy flag for MediCore routing at 09:35 PT; traffic moved to direct hosts for a test cohort.
- Increased ws ping frequency to reduce silent-timeouts for affected connections.

Preliminary result: error rate for the test cohort dropped by ~60% within 3 minutes of the bypass. We still need to clean up fd leaks and run a full host-level postmortem.

Attaching a short snippet of the proxy log and a timeline (see attached in original tar).

— David
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 10:10:02 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: MediCore impact summary and ask for executive support

Team — looping in Marissa and flagging for exec attention.

Customer impact (as of 10:00 PT):
- Scope: 3 of 7 prod clusters saw sustained throughput drop of ~40% during the incident window.
- User-visible sessions affected: ~1.2k active sessions experienced reconnects; eng measured a 7x increase in 5xx responses.
- Business risk: renewal for DC-9821 is 30 days out; customer has flagged this for their CTO.

Customer ask: public-facing RCA and a mitigation timeline. They are asking for consideration of account credits given the magnitude and proximity to renewal.

Requesting: 
1) Exec approval to offer a one-time incident credit (suggested: 10–15% of last quarter's bill) while RCA is completed.
2) Support from leadership on communicating the timeline to the customer's CTO this afternoon.

Lena, Tim — Diego and David are leading the technical mitigation. We will schedule a post-incident bridge for 11:30 PT to walk through the RCA draft and next steps.

— Grace
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@medicorehealth.com>, Tim O'Leary <tim.oleary@medicorehealth.com>, leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 15:02:46 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: MediCore impact summary and ask for executive support

Thank you all for the quick actions. Executive summary for leadership and the customer: 

1) What happened (TL;DR): a proxy config change increased the chunk-aggregation window which, combined with aggressive client retries and a transient file-descriptor pressure on edge-03, produced apparent streaming silence and an elevated 5xx rate for MediCore traffic.

2) Immediate mitigation completed: 
- Rollback of the aggregation timer for the MediCore route (completed 09:32 PT).
- Bypass-proxy routing for affected traffic (enabled 09:35 PT).
- WS ping interval adjusted to reduce silent-timeout churn.

3) Impact: customers in the MediCore cohort saw error rates drop ~60% within minutes; full cluster recovery occurred after hosts were remediated for fd exhaustion.

4) Next steps / owners: 
- SRE (David): full postmortem with timeline, root cause, and host remediation checklist — deliverable EOD tomorrow.
- Engineering (Diego): evaluate guardrails to prevent wide proxy config rollouts without canarying and add automated alerts for chunk-time increases.
- CS (Grace): run customer comms and send a proposed credit offer.

Marissa (VP Eng) — I recommend approving a one-time credit in the 10% range for goodwill while we finalize the RCA and remediation plan. If leadership wants a different number I can adjust the communication.

Lena / Tim: apologies for the disruption; Diego and David are available for a 11:30 PT bridge to go over details. We'll send the official incident summary and timeline after the postmortem.

— Marissa Cole
VP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
